Completan el retrato Naranjito de Triana, el Gallina en los tablaos de Madrid, Calixto Sánchez (Giraldillo de la primera Bienal, 1982), Diego Clavel con su antología de malagueñas, Luis de Córdoba, el Cabrero con sus cabras y sus fandangos, Pansequito (premio a la creatividad en Córdoba), el Turronero (que mezcló pop y flamenco en New jondo), Chiquetete, el Lebrijano («cuando el Lebrijano canta, se moja el agua», García Márquez), Juana la del Revuelo, Aurora Vargas, María Vargas, el Polaco, Antonio Piñana en los cantes mineros, Paco Toronjo en los fandangos y el flamencólogo y cantaor Alfredo Arrebola.

scenes.name: Peterson, Garner, Jamal, Brubeck y el piano para el gran público
scenes.book: Historia del jazz
scenes.desc: Mientras Powell, Monk y Tristano no encajan en el mercado de los cincuenta, otros seis pianistas llevan el piano moderno al gran público sin traicionar el jazz, pese al recelo de una crítica que identifica éxito con haberse «vendido». Oscar Peterson, descubierto por Norman Granz, heredero técnico de Tatum pero más deudor de Nat Cole, es «la voluntad de swing». Nat King Cole, pianista entre Hines y el bop en su trío sin batería, acaba como gran cantante popular. George Shearing populariza un suave sonido de quinteto («Lullaby of Birdland»). Erroll Garner, autodidacta que no leía música, hace sonar el piano como guitarra, batería o arpa (Concert by the Sea, «Misty»). Ahmad Jamal, con su uso del espacio, influye en Miles Davis y anticipa a Bill Evans (But Not for Me). Dave Brubeck, alumno de Milhaud, con Paul Desmond y Time Out legitima los compases inusuales con «Take Five».

scenes.name: El hip hop: medio siglo de historia oral
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.desc: Un género nacido de la imaginación de chavales abandonados entre las ruinas del Bronx de los setenta que sobrevivió a todo (a una generación mayor que lo rechazaba, a las radios que no lo ponían, a los políticos que lo atacaban) hasta convertirse en la música más popular de Estados Unidos. Abrams hizo más de trescientas entrevistas entre 2018 y 2022 a DJs, artistas, productores, ejecutivos y periodistas para contar su origen y su expansión: del Bronx a los demás distritos «como las venas de un plano del metro», del parque al vinilo, a la Costa Oeste con el gangsta rap y el G-funk, al Sur y más allá. «La lírica es, al fin y al cabo, una forma de tradición oral.»

scenes.name: Electroacústica / acusmática
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Nacida en el círculo del GRM y bautizada por Pierre Henry: sustituye los sonidos concretos por otros sintetizados electrónicamente. François Bayle acuña en 1974 «música acusmática»: una música que se genera en un estudio y se proyecta en una sala, como el cine.

scenes.name: Cecil Taylor
scenes.book: Historia del jazz
scenes.desc: El reverso de Coleman: formación de conservatorio (New England Conservatory), Stravinsky y Bartók junto a Ellington, Monk, Waller o Brubeck, y una música más densa, atomista, percusiva y sin romanticismo. Su estilo está formado hacia 1954, antes del free: disonancias, líneas fragmentadas, ataque de martillo neumático, primero sobre standards (Transition, Newport, el Five Spot), luego cada vez más libre en Candid («Cell Walk for Celeste», «como si Charles Ives se bajara en la calle 125») y en Blue Note con Unit Structures y Conquistador! (1966). Trabaja de lavaplatos mientras gana premios; en los setenta se convierte en veterano becado y patrocinado, con conciertos de piano solo como exhibiciones atléticas, música para Baryshnikov y Alvin Ailey y la caja Berlin '88.

scenes.name: Voces del jazz moderno: Ella, Sarah, Carmen y el vocalese
scenes.book: Historia del jazz
scenes.desc: La faceta más ligada a la tradición del jazz de los setenta y ochenta. Norman Granz convierte a Ella Fitzgerald, ya superventas desde la banda de Chick Webb, en una artista mayor con los songbooks dedicados a Porter, Gershwin, Arlen, Ellington y Berlin y los directos de Berlín y Roma; en Pablo la empareja con Basie o Joe Pass. Carmen McRae y Betty Carter prolongan a Billie Holiday con libertades rítmicas casi vanguardistas; Sheila Jordan y Mel Tormé siguen sus propios caminos. El vocalese de Eddie Jefferson y Jon Hendricks pone letra a solos famosos y convierte al cantante en un griot que narra la historia del jazz (Joni Mitchell con «Goodbye Pork Pie Hat», Manhattan Transfer). Bobby McFerrin, imitador de metales y director de orquesta, triunfa con «Don't Worry, Be Happy» y se niega a explotar el éxito.

scenes.name: Big bands de repertorio y orquestas contemporáneas
scenes.book: Historia del jazz
scenes.desc: Desde los cincuenta la big band sobrevive como formación ocasional, banda de ciudad o grupo de repertorio. Sauter y Finegan experimentan con instrumentos raros; Don Ellis, Maynard Ferguson y Buddy Rich se acercan al rock y a los compases extraños. La Thad Jones-Mel Lewis Orchestra toca los lunes en el Village Vanguard desde 1966 por diecisiete dólares y sobrevive a sus fundadores como Vanguard Jazz Orchestra. La big band de Toshiko Akiyoshi (pianista a lo Powell, raíces japonesas, diecisiete instrumentos de viento) y Lew Tabackin domina la costa oeste en los setenta. Gil Evans y su heredera Maria Schneider mantienen la devoción por la orquesta; el Smithsonian, el Lincoln Center y las escuelas convierten la big band en pedagogía histórica, como la orquesta sinfónica.

scenes.name: Sabicas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Navarro (1912-1990), solista desde muy joven. En 1936 acompañó a Carmen Amaya a América, se quedó allí e hizo una gran carrera internacional, famosa por la velocidad de su toque. Con Vicente Escudero, agotado el repertorio, empezó a tocar a lo flamenco canciones hispanoamericanas, tocaba colombianas sin llamarlas así, hizo una versión flamenca de El sitio de Zaragoza y a finales de los sesenta grabó con un guitarrista de rock. Fue mentor de Paco de Lucía en su adolescencia y le aconsejó dejar de imitar al Niño Ricardo.

scenes.name: Sonny Rollins
scenes.book: Historia del jazz
scenes.desc: Frente a las «capas de sonido» de Coltrane, Rollins define el sonido clásico del tenor de la época desde el corazón de la tradición: «que se oiga lo antiguo y lo nuevo». Criado entre Monk, Bud Powell, Parker y Miles, pasa por el quinteto Brown-Roach y mide fuerzas con Coltrane en Tenor Madness. Celebra la improvisación pura, con cadenzas a capela que mezclan arias y canciones pop, un repertorio que va de Kurt Weill a «I'm an Old Cowhand» y temas «para soplar» convertidos en standards («St. Thomas», «Oleo», «Doxy»). Schuller analiza su desarrollo temático, motivo a motivo. Saxophone Colossus, Way Out West en trío sin piano, el Village Vanguard y la Freedom Suite culminan en 1956-1958; luego se retira a practicar en el puente de Williamsburg y vuelve con The Bridge, entre experimentos y regresos a lo conocido.

scenes.name: Benny Carter
scenes.book: Historia del jazz
scenes.desc: Multiinstrumentista (saxo contralto, trompeta, piano, clarinete, voz) cuya versatilidad ha ocultado al arreglista: aprendió orquestación «sobre la marcha» estudiando partituras de la banda de Henderson y sus acordes en bloque para cuatro saxos («Symphony in Riffs», 1933) prefiguran el sonido del swing. Con Johnny Hodges convierte el contralto en una voz principal del jazz. Su vena es lírica, casi schubertiana: piezas de atmósfera («Lonesome Nights», «When Lights Are Low»), melodías cantables y solos de desarrollo temático, pensados como un compositor, dos décadas antes de Sonny Rollins. Tras el JATP escribe para Sarah Vaughan, Ella Fitzgerald y Ray Charles y, pasados los setenta, estrena suites de gran formato.

scenes.name: Antonio, Rosario, Pilar López y las grandes compañías
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: La época de las parejas y los ballets. Antonio Ruiz Soler (1921-1990) bailó con Rosario de 1928 a 1952, con películas en Hollywood y giras por América, y luego se dedicó a la coreografía (El amor brujo, el martinete con yunque); Rosario, discípula del maestro Realito, acabó en la enseñanza. Pilar López, hermana de la Argentinita, formó en su ballet a Farruco, Gades y Mario Maya y añadió los palillos a la siguiriya. El Farruco (1936-1997), autodidacta, fue el patriarca del baile gitano de hombre (Bodas de gloria). El Güito, el más ortodoxo, ganó en 1959 el premio Sarah Bernhardt de París frente a Nureyev. Mario Maya renovó la escena con Camelamos naquerar (1976), con Concha Vargas. Matilde Coral, heredera de Pastora Imperio, maestra de Milagros Menjíbar y María Pagés; Manuela Vargas, «la dama del flamenco»; Tía Juana la del Pipa, que no fue profesional hasta los cuarenta; la Chunga, que bailaba descalza; y Manuela Carrasco, la más importante de su generación, completan el retrato, con las escuelas de Granada (Manolete, Mariquilla) y Córdoba (Concha Calero).

scenes.name: El piano flamenco
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Lorca tocó el piano para la Argentinita y Caracol lo usó en lugar de la guitarra, pero el piano flamenco tiene sus propios nombres. Arturo Pavón (1930), de la familia de los Pavón y de Caracol, formado en el conservatorio, hizo dúo con Luisa Ortega en el tablao Los Canasteros; Pepe Romero (1936-1997) fue el pianista ortodoxo e investigador; Felipe Campuzano, compositor de Andalucía espiritual. Chano Domínguez (1960) viene del jazz y lo une al flamenco; Dorantes (1969), de los Peña de Lebrija, estudió en el conservatorio y Yehudi Menuhin lo llevó a Mont de Marsan; Diego Gallego, de la escuela de Campuzano, ha tocado con Rancapino y Maíta Vende Cá.

scenes.name: El arte jondo: duende y universalidad
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: La tesis de partida: el flamenco, tal como hoy se conoce, tiene poco más de un siglo, pero ha pasado de un desahogo de la Andalucía oprimida, transmitido de generación en generación y disfrutado por unos pocos en reuniones, a un arte mayor aplaudido en los teatros de todo el mundo. La bailaora Cristina Hoyos, en el prólogo, defiende que siga evolucionando con fusiones y mestizajes siempre que no pierda su raíz. Arbelos reúne elogios de voces muy distintas: Manuel de Falla («no hay música más rica, ni más viva en toda Europa»), Stravinski en 1921 («un arte de composición»), Miles Davis en 1950 («es como nuestro blues»), Chick Corea, Unamuno, Pemán, Rubén Darío, Lorca, Juan Ramón Jiménez o Jean Cocteau. Su intemporalidad y universalidad lo ponen a la altura de los clásicos, aunque su cuna sea popular y anónimos sus primeros cultores. Y lo que conmueve al público sin conocimientos previos es el duende: la corriente indefinible que une al intérprete con quien lo escucha. El libro quiere ser una guía sencilla y didáctica para entender lo que se oye en un recital.

scenes.name: Las dinastías de Jerez
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: La ciudad de las bulerías y de las grandes familias gitanas. El Gloria (1893-1954) cantaba saetas y bulerías y creó sus villancicos. Agujeta el Viejo transmitió los cantes de Manuel Torre, y su hijo el Agujetas (1939) tiene la voz rota de los «sonidos negros» de Lorca. Terremoto (1934-1981) fue indispensable en los festivales de los sesenta por siguiriyas y bulerías; el Sordera (1927-2001) brilló en los tablaos de Madrid y dejó una dinastía; el Chocolate (1931), voz de la escuela de Torre, ganó el Giraldillo de la Bienal de 1986 y un Grammy Latino en 2002. Tío Juane cantaba martinetes forjando una herradura y la Paquera (1934) tenía una voz de enorme potencia. José Mercé (1955), de la dinastía de Paco la Luz y cantaor de la compañía de Gades, es a comienzos del siglo XXI el cantaor de más éxito, por unir la raíz jonda con la música de su tiempo. Siguen el Capullo, maestro del compás, Diego Carrasco, cuyo ritmo buscan Camarón o Morente, y la Macanita, la gran cantaora joven de Jerez.

scenes.name: Las bamberas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: El cante que acompañaba el vaivén del columpio, la bamba, en las fiestas campesinas al acabar la cosecha o en las fiestas patronales, con ritmo de soleá lenta. Como todos los cantes folclóricos andaluces que se aflamencaron entre finales del XIX y la primera mitad del XX, su jondura depende del intérprete: unas sevillanas de Camarón son flamencas; las de un coro rociero, canción folclórica. Su creadora indiscutible fue la Niña de los Peines, y Camarón cantó por bamberas «La leyenda del tiempo» de Lorca.

scenes.name: La rumba
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: El cante de ida y vuelta más estudiado, tan parecido al tango que confunde a los investigadores. Según Papa Wemba su melodía es centroafricana, de Zaire: viajó con la trata de esclavos a Cuba y de allí a España. La aportación más flamenca fue la de Pepe de la Matrona, que vivió en Cuba a mediados de la década de 1910 (Recuerdos de La Habana, 1914). La rumba catalana tiene su estilo propio, con el Pescaílla, marido de Lola Flores, y Peret, y su toque rapidísimo «del ventilador». Poco apreciada por los flamencos, ha crecido con la salsa entre el público joven; Paco de Lucía tuvo su primer gran éxito con la rumba «Entre dos aguas» y la «Macarena» de Los del Río batió todos los récords. Su baile es sensual y provocador.

scenes.name: La escuela gaditana
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Los cantaores de Cádiz, herederos del Mellizo, dueños de las cantiñas, los tanguillos y las alegrías. Aurelio Sellés (1887-1974) fue uno de sus puntales y dominó cantiñas, siguiriyas, soleares y malagueñas. Pericón de Cádiz (1901-1980) contó su vida en Las mil y una historias de Pericón. La Perla de Cádiz (1925-1975) recreó los estilos de su tierra. Chano Lobato (1927) es el «dueño del compás»: acompañó a Antonio, Matilde Coral y Manuela Vargas y desde los ochenta canta como solista. Les siguen Rancapino, continuador de Aurelio; Chaquetón, de la saga de los Chaqueta y en la línea del Mellizo; Mariana Cornejo, popular por un anuncio cantado por tanguillos; y Juanito Villar, salido de las comparsas de carnaval, que grabó con Paco Cepero.

scenes.name: Villancicos y zambombas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cantes navideños sobre el nacimiento del «Niño Manuel», de remoto origen profano (hay quien los deriva del zéjel árabe), que el legendario Niño Gloria de Jerez adaptó al compás de bulerías, tangos y tanguillos; sus villancicos los conocen todos los artistas. José Mercé los recreó con gran jondura en la serie Así canta nuestra tierra por Navidad (doce volúmenes), con el tocaor Parrilla de Jerez y el aula de folclore de la Cátedra de Flamencología. En Jerez se celebran por Navidad las zambombas: reuniones familiares en patios de vecinos o bodegas donde se canta en corro por bulerías y tangos, se baila en el centro y se comen pestiños.

scenes.name: Las bulerías
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: El cante festero por excelencia, con el compás de la soleá mucho más acelerado; nacido a comienzos del siglo XX (Mairena atribuye al Loco Mateo, en el XIX, el remate acelerado de las soleares). Tiene dos centros: Cádiz, más larga y suave, y Jerez, más corta y bulliciosa, «la ciudad de los gitanos» de Lorca, donde hasta las piedras cantan por bulerías y el soniquete se lleva en la sangre. El nombre se discute: burla, bolero o bulla. Su métrica lo admite todo, coplas de soleá, seguidillas o canciones (en Utrera, letras de canciones ajenas): un buen cantaor podría cantar por bulerías la guía telefónica. Cierra cualquier festival en el fin de fiesta, y quien la domina en el cante, el baile o el toque domina todo el flamenco.

scenes.name: Los cantes de ida y vuelta: colombiana, guajira, vidalita, milonga
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cantes folclóricos hispanoamericanos (rumba, milonga, colombiana, guajira, vidalita) aflamencados por la manera de cantarlos en Andalucía; fáciles de cantar, no se consideran cante jondo. Llegaron en la última década del XIX y se difundieron desde los años treinta: son la última gran incorporación al flamenco. La idea de que eran cantes andaluces que fueron a América y volvieron es pura mitopoética. Sabicas contaba que él y Vicente Escudero, con muchos contratos en América y el repertorio flamenco agotado, empezaron a tocar esas canciones «con este aire nuestro». La colombiana no viene de América: la creó Pepe Marchena en los treinta, con enorme éxito; Carmen Amaya fue la primera en cantarla y bailarla, Sabicas la tocaba sin nombrarla por vergüenza y Juanito Valderrama popularizó la suya en los cincuenta. La guajira, de Cuba, fue la primera en llegar y la que mejor se adaptó (en Cádiz se cantaban «guajiras festeras» por bulerías); sus coplas son décimas. La vidalita, del norte argentino y triste, la recuperaron en los noventa jóvenes como Mayte Martín; la milonga pampeana la trajo Pepa Oro en compás de tangos, Chacón la remataba por tanguillos y Pepe de la Matrona la grabó. Hay dos discos fundamentales: Cantes de ida y vuelta (Junta de Andalucía, 1985, con Menese, José Mercé y Luis de Córdoba) y Dos mundos cantan (Expo 92, con Valderrama, Rocío Jurado y Chano Lobato).

scenes.name: Las saetas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cante dolido que solo se canta en Semana Santa, al paso de las imágenes, a palo seco o con cornetas y tambores, por martinetes, siguiriyas (las más comunes), soleares, cañas o polos, con coplas de exaltación religiosa que exigen gran potencia de voz. Nace a finales del XIX en Cádiz: Enrique el Mellizo y sus hijos detenían al Nazareno desde los cuatro balcones de su casa con sus saetas. A él se atribuye la saeta por siguiriyas, que desarrolló Manuel Centeno en el siglo XX. Manuel Torre, el Niño Gloria, la Niña de los Peines, Manolo Caracol y Antonio Mairena eran esperados en Semana Santa para cantarlas sin amplificación desde un balcón a la altura de las imágenes; Manuel Mairena grabó un vía crucis entero. Un equipo francés grabó en directo a los saeteros de Jerez, Arcos y Lebrija en la Semana Santa de 1993 para la colección Flamenco vivo.

scenes.name: Demófilo y los Machado
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Antonio Machado y Álvarez, Demófilo, fue el primer autor español que dedicó un libro entero al flamenco: la Colección de cantes flamencos recogidos y anotados (1881), piedra angular de la flamencología moderna; escribió también sobre las saetas y dirigió la revista El Folclore Andaluz (1882-1883). Sus hijos, los poetas Antonio y Manuel Machado (autor de Cante hondo), heredaron la afición, y sus coplas se cantan a menudo sin que los cantaores sepan que son versos cultos. Calixto Sánchez dedicó a Antonio Machado un disco en 2001, y José Menese hizo suyas las letras de Francisco Moreno Galván.

scenes.name: La farruca y el garrotín
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cantes aflamencados de fuera de Andalucía. La farruca, gallega, llegó a Cádiz con los comerciantes gallegos del XIX y es más baile que cante; la popularizó Manuel Torre a principios del XX y hoy casi solo la canta Pepe Menese, con una letra de Moreno Galván que se hizo himno en la Transición. Su baile, viril, lo creó Faíco; Carmen Amaya lo bailó vestida de hombre, Falla lo incluyó en El sombrero de tres picos y la versión de Antonio Gades en la película de Los Tarantos, la última de Carmen Amaya, se enseña hoy en las academias. El garrotín viene del folclore asturiano y lo hicieron suyo los gitanos de Lleida; lo difundieron Carmen Amaya y la Niña de los Peines, que lo cantaba con aire de tangos, Faíco hizo sus coreografías y Blas Vega recogió una copla antigua cantada por el Chaparro en la Magna antología del cante flamenco.

scenes.name: Los fandangos de Huelva
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Huelva reclama la cuna del fandango andaluz y es la provincia con más estilos: las antologías recogen más de treinta y cinco, locales (Encinasola, el Alosno, Cabezas Rubias, Calañas, el Andévalo, Valverde del Camino) y personales, creados por profesionales como Paco Isidro, Pepe Rebollo, el Comía, Antonio Rengel, Pérez de Guzmán y Paco Toronjo; de fuera dejaron su sello el Gloria, Macandé, el Carbonerillo y Manolo Caracol. Paco Toronjo, fijo en los festivales desde finales de los sesenta y en las bienales de Sevilla, les dio una jondura difícil de imitar. El baile, de pareja y galanteo, se ve ya poco.

scenes.name: Los cantes de Levante o de las minas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Nacidos del trabajo en las minas del siglo XIX en las sierras de Cartagena y La Unión y en Linares, La Carolina y Andújar: cantes de dolor profundo sobre la mina, sus accidentes y los compañeros muertos, hechos con fandangos regionales, murcianas, malagueñas y el cante de madrugá de los mineros. La taranta, el más significativo, tiene dos estilos, el de Linares (Gabriel Moreno, Carmen Linares) y el de La Unión (Encarnación Fernández, Pepe Cros), y Camarón le puso dulzura; el taranto, almeriense, tiene compás porque nació para el baile de Carmen Amaya en los cuarenta, con el Ciego de la Playa y Pedro el Morato. La cartagenera, de temas más urbanos, la fijó Antonio Chacón a finales del XIX y la cantaron Cayetano Muriel, Manuel Centeno, Manuel Torre y la Niña de los Peines. La minera se atribuye a Rojo el Alpargatero, Antonio Grau Mora, que hacia 1885 abrió en La Unión una posada que acabó en café cantante y oía cantar a los mineros de madrugada: es el gran creador de los cantes mineros. Las granaínas, de Frasquito Yerbabuena y sobre todo Chacón, son un cante casi barroco hoy cargado de vibratos operísticos. Sin minas, los concursos de Linares y La Unión mantienen vivos estos cantes.

scenes.name: Las cantiñas: alegrías, caracoles, mirabrás y romeras
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cantes alegres de la bahía de Cádiz, en compás de soleá y muy ligados al baile, que arranca majestuoso y va ganando fuerza hasta desplantes electrizantes. Nacen probablemente de la jotilla gaditana, hermanada con la jota aragonesa por la resistencia común contra Napoleón, de ahí las letras sobre la guerra y el mar; la leyenda atribuye su creación a Enrique el Mellizo, que oyó a una muchacha cantar jotas con un ciego. Tomaron identidad en la segunda mitad del XIX. Hay cantiñas del Pinini de Utrera y Lebrija y de Córdoba; la rosa ya no se canta. Las alegrías, al principio baile de mujer sola, se hicieron más lentas a comienzos del XX y empiezan con el «tirititrán» que, según Chano Lobato, inventó Pericón de Cádiz al olvidar la letra; las cantaron el Mellizo, Ignacio Ezpeleta, Aurelio Sellés, Manolo Vargas y Pericón. Los caracoles, de Tío José el Granaíno (picador del Chiclanero), los recreó Chacón y triunfaron en Madrid («la gran calle de Alcalá»). El mirabrás son alegrías largas (José Menese, con letras de Moreno Galván), y las romeras se atribuyen al Granaíno o a una cantaora llamada la Romera. Hoy el gran intérprete es Chano Lobato.

scenes.name: Los tangos, tientos y marianas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Con bulerías y cantiñas, el gran cante festero: letras de vida, amor y muerte con cierta ligereza, ritmo vivo y pegadizo fácil de seguir con palmas, y un baile sensual. Cádiz y Sevilla se disputan su paternidad, pero los hay en toda Andalucía y en Extremadura; Triana tiene el estilo del Titi y Jerez su propio sello. Su origen musical se discute: Mairena los tenía por cante básico gitano; los estudios recientes los llevan a Cuba y las habaneras llegadas a Sevilla y Cádiz en la segunda mitad del XIX; los granadinos defienden una raíz morisca (el disco Granada canta por tangos recoge trece estilos, entre ellos los de la morería). Manuel Ríos Ruiz concluye que no se sabe con certeza. La Niña de los Peines se hizo inmortal con su copla «Péinate tú con mis peines». Del tango nacen los tientos, más pausados y solemnes, que cantaron primero el Mellizo y el Marrurro y se popularizaron a comienzos del XX, y la mariana, que difundió Bernardo el de los Lobitos y hoy casi solo canta Pepe Menese con letras de Moreno Galván.

scenes.name: Las soleares
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: La madre del cante y uno de sus pilares, independiente de cualquier otro ritmo; los cantaores la consideran «el toro bravo del arte jondo». Coplas solemnes y sentenciosas de tres o cuatro octosílabos, unidas por la guitarra, que suelen rematarse por bulerías; muy apropiadas para el baile de mujer. Se desarrolló al sur del Guadalquivir desde los jaleos festivos: la primera mención es de la Andonda en Triana hacia 1840, una cantaora temible contemporánea del Fillo, y tomó su forma actual entre 1875 y 1915. Las mujeres fueron clave en su creación y transmisión (la Andonda, Mercedes la Serneta, Fernanda de Utrera, Carmen Linares). Hay soleares de Triana (la Andonda, Silverio, Fernando el de Triana, la Niña de los Peines, Tomás Pavón, Mairena), de Alcalá, más solemnes (Joaquín el de la Paula, Juan Talega), de Utrera (la Serneta, el Pinini, María Peña, Fernanda), de Cádiz y el Puerto, más jondas (Enrique Butrón, el Mellizo, Paquirri el Guanté), de Jerez, breves y llenas de melismas (Curro Frijones, José Illanda, Juan Mojama, Tío José de Paula, Manuel Torre) y de Córdoba, más pausadas.

scenes.name: Las siguiriyas, livianas y serranas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Una de las expresiones más dramáticas y de los palos más importantes: sin siguiriyas y soleares el flamenco no sería lo que es. Un quejío entero de lamentos que no admite medias tintas («con las siguiriyas no se puede vender la burra»), con coplas trágicas de cuatro versos (6, 6, 10 y 6 sílabas), muchas sobre la muerte de los seres queridos, y falsetas lentas que suenan a campanas a muerto. Lorca la describió como un grito terrible que divide el paisaje en dos; Tía Anica la Piriñaca decía que cuando la cantaba a gusto la boca le sabía a sangre. La cantaban ya el Planeta (la de la Luna, la más antigua conocida) y el Fillo; luego Manuel Torre, Silverio, Paco la Luz, Cagancho, el Nitri, Curro Dulce, el Loco Mateo, el Mellizo, Terremoto de Jerez (que cantó toda la noche por siguiriyas con su madre muerta en brazos) y Juan Talega; hoy el Chocolate y José Menese. Antonio Mairena grabó unas cuarenta y cinco formas: es el siguiriyero más importante. Sus escuelas son Jerez y los Puertos, Cádiz y Triana. En el baile la difundió Vicente Escudero y Pilar López le añadió los palillos. La liviana, cante de campo, caminos y bandoleros, prepara la voz para la serrana, a la que Silverio dio brillo y con la que se remata por siguiriyas.

scenes.name: La caña, el polo y la petenera
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Tres cantes de la familia de la soleá. La caña, con ayes más arrastrados, se sitúa en la serranía de Ronda (un viajero inglés la oyó allí en 1830) o en la voz árabe gaunia, «canción»; la cantaron el Fillo, Tío José el Granaíno, Antonio Chacón, Pepe de la Matrona y Rafael Romero el Gallina, y hoy se usa más para el baile solemne. El polo se cantaba tras la caña, con la misma métrica; el de Tobalo, su supuesto creador, aparece ya en Estébanez Calderón y hoy se usa en la soleá apolá; Enrique Morente grabó el de Chacón. La petenera, melancólica y de origen incierto, se atribuye a una mujer de Paterna de la Ribera, «la perdición de los hombres», o a los sefardíes de los Balcanes; los gitanos la evitaron porque traía mala suerte. La cantaron la Niña de los Peines, Naranjito de Triana, Rafael Romero, Fosforito y hoy Pepe Menese.

scenes.name: Los cantes de Málaga: malagueñas, rondeñas, jaberas y verdiales
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Después de Sevilla y Cádiz, Málaga es la provincia con más variedad de cantes. La malagueña, cante libre, sin medida y sin baile, de rico toque, ha influido en las granaínas y en todos los cantes minero-levantinos. Nació en Álora (las malagueñas perotas) a partir de los fandangos abandolaos, acompañados de bandola; tras los anónimos y los de Cipriano Pitana, Francisco Jiménez y Joaquín Tabaco, Juan Breva le dio identidad propia, y Lorca escribió de su trino. Su esplendor es la segunda mitad del XIX, con el Canario, la Trini, Baldomero Pacheco y Fosforito el Viejo; también firmaron malagueñas el Mellizo, único gitano creador de una (inspirada en el prefacio de la misa), y Chacón. Diego Clavel recogió treinta y una en los noventa. La rondeña, de principios del XIX y de la tierra del Tobalo, es la pieza con que muchos guitarristas abren sus conciertos; la jabera, ruda y difícil, debe su nombre a una vendedora de habas y está casi perdida; los verdiales, de probable raíz morisca, apenas han cambiado y conservan la panda con violín, panderos, chinchines y cañas para la fiesta de san Juan.

scenes.name: Los tanguillos de Cádiz
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Vinculados al carnaval de Cádiz, son el soporte de chirigotas, coros y murgas; cantados en grupo pierden su naturaleza flamenca, que es individual, aunque como baile la conservan. Hay constancia de los «tangos graciosos» del barrio de La Viña en 1779, en la tonadilla La anónima de Tomás Abril, y el tango americano o de negros terminó de formarlos. Letras jocosas y satíricas: «el chiste ingenuo y feliz enfrente de la tragedia jonda del quejío» (Emilio Jiménez Díaz). Aurelio y Pericón de Cádiz, Manuel Vargas y la Perla los grabaron en la primera mitad del siglo XX, y hasta Mairena dejó dos. Chano Lobato, su mayor cultor, los elevó a cante noble y recrea la venta de los cuadros que popularizó Pericón.

scenes.name: Las tonás: martinetes, carceleras y deblas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cantes sin acompañamiento, prueba de su antigüedad, en cuartetas octosílabas de intensa carga dramática y origen gitano indiscutible: son crónicas de la miseria, la cárcel y la persecución. Demófilo ya las daba en 1881 por «cantes viejos casi caídos en desuso»; en el siglo XIX hubo entre veintisiete y treinta y cuatro, cada una con el nombre de su creador. La más antigua es la de Tío Luis el de la Juliana, aguador y primer cantaor del que hay noticia (segunda mitad del siglo XVIII), conservada por Antonio Chacón y recreada por Pepe de la Matrona; se le atribuye también la toná de los pajaritos, que recuerda la tonada sefardí de los bilbilicos. Los martinetes toman el nombre del martillo de la fragua, aunque es difícil cantar mientras se forja: Tío Juane de Jerez montaba una fragua en escena en los setenta y ochenta, y Antonio el Bailarín creó su baile con martillo y yunque; la familia fragüera más antigua es la de los Cantorales de Cádiz, que Silverio visitaba. Las carceleras cantan la prisión y servían para pasar mensajes en romaní desde las rejas. La debla, único palo con nombre romaní («diosa»), es religiosa, casi perdida y muy difícil; llegó a hoy por Tomás Pavón en los cuarenta y la recuperó Antonio Mairena.

scenes.name: Las sevillanas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Nacen de las seguidillas castellanas, que en Sevilla se hicieron más vivas y fáciles de repetir: cuatro coplas para bailar en pareja un galanteo, con temas andaluces, amorosos o rocieros (corraleras, rocieras, bíblicas, de feria, marineras, romeras). Lorca recogió una del siglo XVIII. Su gran auge comercial llegó en los setenta, con millones de discos que daban envidia a los flamencos; las han grabado con jondura Manuel Vallejo, la Niña de los Peines, la Paquera de Jerez, el Turronero, Chiquetete y Camarón.

scenes.name: El fandango
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Muy apreciado por su musicalidad y fácil de interpretar, no es un palo básico pero no es menor: la vieja división entre cantes grandes y chicos está obsoleta, y la jondura la pone el intérprete, no la antigüedad del palo. Canto para bailar de origen muy antiguo e incierto (Corominas lo deriva del portugués fado; hay quien le ve un lejano origen árabe), aparece por escrito en un entremés de 1705 y lo describe el deán Manuel Martí en 1712; en el siglo XIX fue el cante y baile nacional español, y a finales de siglo se aflamencó en Andalucía y dejó de bailarse. De él salen las granaínas, las malagueñas y los cantes de Levante, y hay fandangos propios en Lucena, Cabra, Puente Genil, Jaén, Granada o Almería. Su apogeo en la ópera flamenca lo desprestigió tanto que a cantaores como Pepe Menese les parece un insulto que se lo pidan; desde los años ochenta se revaloriza.

facts.title: Naked in Bed with Mick Jagger – Angela Bowie's 1990 TV Claim, Denied Then Partially Walked Back
facts.body: On May 4, 1990, David Bowie's ex-wife Angela appeared on the Joan Rivers Show, newly freed from a 10-year gag order after their divorce. She stated on national television: "I caught him in bed with Mick Jagger — and yes, they were naked." Bowie was a professed bisexual during the 1970s. Mick Jagger immediately dismissed the claim as "rubbish," and Bowie's lawyer sent an open letter stating that "any implication that there was ever a gay affair between Mick Jagger and David Bowie is an absolute fabrication." Within a week, Angela was qualifying her statement. By her 1993 autobiography, the account had evolved: she had walked in, assumed they had been having sex, and that was her honest belief, but she had no proof. An additional complication: Angela may have had her own affair with Jagger during the marriage, possibly inspiring the Rolling Stones song "Angie" — or, in another rumor, that "Angie" referred to David himself using a nickname. "Did they spend the night together? Yes. Were they naked? Apparently. Was it sexual? Who knows?"
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: David Bowie

facts.title: Lost Interview Tape (1990)
facts.body: In 1990, prior to the ongoing history show, the speaker had a 30-minute, face-to-face interview with David Bowie during his Tin Machine years. The speaker was so overwhelmed by Bowie's presence, focusing on his various personas, that he forgot to unpause his tape machine, resulting in no recording. "And I don't remember what I asked him. I don't remember what he said because I was just like, this is Bowie."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: OGHONM 1000th Episode: The Q&A From the Live Recording
facts.name: David Bowie

facts.title: Rumored Affair with Mick Jagger (1990)
facts.body: A long-standing rumor regarding an affair between David Bowie and Mick Jagger originated on the Joan Rivers show on May 4, 1990. Angela Bowie, David's ex-wife (married 1970-1980), claimed on the show, after a decade-long gag order from her divorce settlement expired, that she caught them naked in bed together. Bowie had professed bisexuality in the 1970s, which lent some credibility to the story. Mick Jagger vehemently denied the claims, and Bowie's lawyer issued a letter calling any implication of a gay affair an "absolute fabrication." Angela Bowie later revised her story in her 1993 autobiography, stating she "just assumed they were having sex" and lacked proof. "I caught David in bed with Mick Jagger."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: David Bowie

facts.title: Charismatic Interview Subject (1990, Tin Machine era)
facts.body: In 1990, during his Tin Machine years, David Bowie exhibited a profound level of charisma in an interview, similar to Bono. He maintained intense eye contact, creating an immersive experience for the interviewer, who was so overwhelmed that they forgot to record the conversation. Years later, when reminded of the incident, Bowie directly yet humorously acknowledged the error. "The only other person with that level of charisma that I ever talked to was David Bowie."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The 1000th Episode of the Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: George Harrison on Ringo's Death Threat (1990)
facts.body: In 1990, George Harrison recounted a specific death threat against Ringo Starr during The Beatles' 1964 Montreal visit. He stated that a Montreal newspaper reported someone intended to kill Ringo, possibly because they disliked his nose or because he was perceived as "the most British of the Beatles." "A Montreal newspaper reported that somebody was going to kill Ringo because they didn't like his nose or something, because he was probably the most British of the Beatles."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Beatles

facts.title: Kurt Throwing Bottles at Drummer Chad Channing – Live at Lee's Palace, Toronto (April 16, 1990)
facts.body: By spring 1990, Kurt was profoundly unhappy with Chad Channing's drumming. At Lee's Palace in Toronto on April 16, 1990 — the band's first Toronto show — Kurt began hurling glass bottles at the wall behind Chad; the audience followed suit. A recording of the one-hour set captures the glass shattering behind the kit. "Kurt started throwing glass bottles at the wall behind Chad and the audience followed."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Dave Grohl Joined Nirvana Because His Band's Bassist Broke Up with His Girlfriend (1990)
facts.body: Dave dropped out of high school to tour with DC punk band Scream for about three years. In the summer of 1990, bassist Skeater Thompson flaked out mid-tour in Los Angeles over the loss of his girlfriend, canceling multiple shows. Dave was left penniless (temporarily crashing with three female mud wrestlers) and doing cash tiling work for food money. He called Melvins leader King Buzzo (Kurt Cobain's idol), whom he'd met in Europe, who told him Kurt had a band needing a drummer. Dave flew to Seattle on September 21, 1990; four days later he auditioned and passed. Dave later wrote a song about Skeater Thompson called "Just Another Story About Skeater Thompson," available only on a cassette-only release made under the name "Late" in late 1990, titled *Pocket Watch*. "Dave has never forgotten Skeater Thompson and how thankful he is that Skeater had such bad girlfriend trouble."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Dave Grohl's Audition and Joining (1990)
facts.body: After his previous band Scream disbanded, Dave Grohl was connected with Nirvana through Buzz Osborne of The Melvins. Grohl auditioned at the Dutchman rehearsal space in Seattle on September 25, 1990, and secured the drumming position instantly, completing the lineup that would become one of the most successful rock bands of the 1990s. facts.title: Dave Grohl Joined Nirvana Because His Band's Bassist Broke Up with His Girlfriend (1990)
facts.body: Dave dropped out of high school to tour with DC punk band Scream for about three years. In the summer of 1990, bassist Skeater Thompson flaked out mid-tour in Los Angeles over the loss of his girlfriend, canceling multiple shows. Dave was left penniless (temporarily crashing with three female mud wrestlers) and doing cash tiling work for food money. He called Melvins leader King Buzzo (Kurt Cobain's idol), whom he'd met in Europe, who told him Kurt had a band needing a drummer. Dave flew to Seattle on September 21, 1990; four days later he auditioned and passed. Dave later wrote a song about Skeater Thompson called "Just Another Story About Skeater Thompson," available only on a cassette-only release made under the name "Late" in late 1990, titled *Pocket Watch*. "Dave has never forgotten Skeater Thompson and how thankful he is that Skeater had such bad girlfriend trouble."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Last Commercial Flight into East Germany (October 2, 1990)
facts.body: On October 2, 1990, U2 boarded a British Airways flight into Tegal Airport in Berlin, which was the final commercial flight to land in East Germany before its official reunification with West Germany at midnight that day. The band traveled to Berlin to begin working on ideas for their next album at Hansa Studios. "On October 2nd, 1990, you two, boarded a British Airways flight into Tegal Airport in Berlin. That was the last commercial flight into East Germany before East Germany ceased to exist."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Golden Age of Hip Hop (1990-1996)
facts.body: The period between 1990 and 1995-1996 is considered the greatest era in hip hop history, marked by seminal albums from artists like Public Enemy, Ice Cube, Nas, Notorious B.I.G., and Tupac, leading up to the Wu Tang Clan's debut. This era saw the emergence of various rapper archetypes, from solo artists to large "clans" of eight or ten members. "Fue posiblemente la mejor época de la historia del hip hop."

facts.title: Decline by 1990
facts.body: By 1990, pop music was in decline, as the generation that enjoyed artists like New Kids on the Block, Tiffany, and Debbie Gibson had aged out of their pop phase. They were not interested in artists like Whitney Houston or Fleetwood Mac, and the genre's credibility suffered from the Milli Vanilli Grammys scandal. "Meanwhile, pop music had been in the descendant."

facts.title: The Warehouse Riot (1990)
facts.body: On March 20, 1990, an autograph session scheduled for Depeche Mode at The Warehouse record store in Los Angeles escalated into a riot. A crowd of 20,000 to 25,000 people, who had been gathering for two days, surged forward upon the band's arrival, creating dangerous pressure on the store's plate-glass windows. The event was canceled by police, leading to widespread destruction, including bricks, rocks, and bottles being thrown, neon signs destroyed, and parts of the building damaged. The incident required 150 LAPD officers in riot gear, resulted in seven hospitalizations, and left the record store with a $25,000 cleanup bill. "When the crowd realized that the autograph session was canceled, they went nuts, bricks and rocks and bottles started flying."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 5
facts.name: Depeche Mode

facts.title: World Violation Tour (May 28, 1990)
facts.body: Depeche Mode commenced their global tour for the "Violator" album in Pensacola, Florida. The tour comprised 88 sold-out gigs worldwide, solidifying their status as one of the biggest bands globally by its conclusion. "A few months later, on May 28th, 1990, Depeche Mode began their world violation tour in Pensacola, Florida."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour
facts.name: Depeche Mode

facts.title: Post-World Violation Tour Hiatus and Fan Intrusion (1990-1992)
facts.body: After the demanding World Violation Tour, Depeche Mode took an 18-month break. During this period, Dave Gahan faced extreme fan intrusion, having to move twice because fans frequently appeared on his lawn, with one even hiring a private detective to find his home address. "Once that tour wrapped up, Depeche Mode took a little time off and they needed it."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour
facts.name: Depeche Mode

facts.title: Los Angeles Autograph Session Riot (1990)
facts.body: On March 20, 1990, a riot at an autograph session in Los Angeles marked the first indication that a fourth rock cycle was beginning. This event occurred 13 years and 10 days after the Sex Pistols' contract signing and 26 years after The Beatles' Ed Sullivan appearance. "The first indication that a fourth cycle was starting was at a riot at a de Pesh mode autograph session in Los Angeles on March 20th of 1990."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History of Alt Rock Chapter: 14
facts.name: Depeche Mode

facts.title: Violator Autograph Session Riot (March 20, 1990)
facts.body: On March 20, 1990, an autograph session for Depeche Mode's album *Violator* at The Warehouse music store in Los Angeles escalated into an infamous riot. Thousands of fans overwhelmed private security, prompting the LAPD to call a tactical alert and dispatch 20 police units, with additional ambulances later required. The event resulted in multiple arrests, injuries including one person being crushed, and damage to a Fox News microwave van, forcing the band to leave early. "One of their stores in Los Angeles was the scene of the infamous Depeche Mode riot during an autograph session for the violator Ravel on March 20th 1990."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History of the Record Store
facts.name: Depeche Mode

facts.title: Merchandise Sales Success (1990)
facts.body: Depeche Mode achieved remarkable merchandise sales in 1990, earning $1.5 million over just two nights in Los Angeles, showcasing the significant growth of the band merch industry. "In 1990, the Pesh Mode made $1.5 million over just two nights in Los Angeles."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Depeche Mode

facts.body: The first indication of this cycle was the Depeche Mode riot on March 20, 1990, leading to a quick pickup in spring 1990 with the rise of Madchester and Grunge. facts.title: Jeremy Dell's Suicide Attempts (April-June 1990)
facts.body: Between April and June 1990, Jeremy Dell attempted suicide at least three times, utilizing different methods including pills, threatening to jump off a church roof, and making threats to shoot himself. This history indicated a clear need for additional help and treatment that he evidently did not receive. "Between April and June 1990, he attempted suicide at least three times, pills, threatening to jump off the roof of a church, and a threat to shoot himself."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Pearl Jam

facts.title: Escalating Threats and Suicide Talk (Nov-Dec 1990)
facts.body: In November 1990, Jeremy Dell began casually discussing suicide with classmates. The following month, he was again on in-school suspension for making more threats against teachers, had stolen money from a cash box at a basketball game, continued talking about suicide, and made a specific threat about "blowing the head off a particular teacher." These incidents marked a clear escalation of his troubling behavior and mental state. "The following month, he was back on in-school suspension for making more threats against teachers."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Pearl Jam

facts.title: Reformation Proposal (1990)
facts.body: Mick Jones proposed reforming The Clash around 1990. However, Joe Strummer's insistence on the original late 70s/early 80s lineup (Joe, Mick, Paul Simonon, Topper Headon or Terry Chimes) and their former manager Bernie Rhodes (who had tried to sue them) led to the other members refusing the plan, and the reformation never occurred. "Mick Jones came calling, suggesting that he and Joe reform the clash."

facts.title: End of 1980s Imperial Phase (1990)
facts.body: The release of "Oh Father" marked the end of Madonna's 1980s imperial phase. Its peak at number 20 in the first week of January 1990 was her first single since 1984 to miss the Top 10, let alone the Top 5. "Oh, father peaked at number 20, the first week of January 1990, her first single since 1984 to miss the Top 10, let alone the Top 5."

facts.title: "The Immaculate Collection" as Narrative Reshaper (1990)
facts.body: Madonna used "The Immaculate Collection" as a "bookend" to her 1980s imperial phase, confidently shaping the narrative of her first decade by including classics like "Into the Groove" (despite its non-single status in the US) and intentionally omitting several number one and top five hits like "Angel," "Dress You Up," "True Blue," "Who's That Girl," and "Causing a Commotion." "I regard the immaculate collection as the bookend to Madonna's 80s imperial phase, her last flex, with regal confidence she was already shaping the narrative of her first decade, discarding what was expendable and enshrining her class."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

facts.title: End of 1980s Imperial Phase (1990)
facts.body: The release of "Oh Father" marked the end of Madonna's 1980s imperial phase. Its peak at number 20 in the first week of January 1990 was her first single since 1984 to miss the Top 10, let alone the Top 5. "Oh, father peaked at number 20, the first week of January 1990, her first single since 1984 to miss the Top 10, let alone the Top 5."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.episode: Material Girl in an Imperial World Edition Part 2
facts.name: Madonna

facts.title: "The Immaculate Collection" as Narrative Reshaper (1990)
facts.body: Madonna used "The Immaculate Collection" as a "bookend" to her 1980s imperial phase, confidently shaping the narrative of her first decade by including classics like "Into the Groove" (despite its non-single status in the US) and intentionally omitting several number one and top five hits like "Angel," "Dress You Up," "True Blue," "Who's That Girl," and "Causing a Commotion." "I regard the immaculate collection as the bookend to Madonna's 80s imperial phase, her last flex, with regal confidence she was already shaping the narrative of her first decade, discarding what was expendable and enshrining her class."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.episode: Material Girl in an Imperial World Edition Part 2
facts.name: Madonna

facts.body: By 1990, techno diversified into two distinct paths: a commercial, more danceable, and club-oriented style (represented by "Techno 2: The Next Generation") and a harder, more underground, minimalist style championed by artists like Underground Resistance and Richie Hawtin. facts.title: Joining Nirvana (1990)
facts.body: In September 1990, after his band Scream unexpectedly broke up mid-tour, leaving him stranded in Los Angeles, Dave Grohl sought drumming opportunities by calling his friend Buzz Osborne of The Melvins. Osborne facilitated a connection to Nirvana, leading to Grohl's successful audition at the Dutchman rehearsal space in Seattle on September 25, 1990, where he "got the gig instantly." "The day Dave Grohl unexpectedly got the gig with this weird little band called Nirvana, September 25th, 1990."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 5
facts.name: Dave Grohl

facts.title: Pre-Nirvana Demos (1990)
facts.body: Dave Grohl began recording his own song demos as early as 1990, even before he officially joined Nirvana. These early recordings showcased his ambition beyond being a drummer and eventually led to the release of his cassette-only album "Pocket Watch" under the moniker Late. "Dave recorded some demos as far back as 1990, even before he was with Nirvana."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Dave Grohl

facts.title: Harling Talks AD Alias (1990)
facts.body: In the summer of 1990, while still with Scream, Dave Grohl recorded new demos on his own, creating the alias "Harling Talks Angel Divine," or "Harling Talks AD" for short. With assistance from Barrett Jones and Toss Newyn Huizen, he recorded experimental material that he never expected to go anywhere, and there was never a "Harling Talks show." "Dave created a new alias, he called Harling Talks Angel Divine or Harling Talks AD for short."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Ultra-Deep Background on Dave Grohl: Part 2
facts.name: Dave Grohl

facts.title: Joining Nirvana (1990)
facts.body: A few months after recording his Harling Talks AD demos, Dave Grohl received a call to audition for Nirvana. Scream had broken up over "girlfriend troubles" while on tour, leaving Dave stranded in Los Angeles. Buzz Osborne of The Melvins, who was idolized by Kurt Cobain, recommended Dave for the open drummer position. Dave flew to Seattle, arriving on Friday, September 21, 1990, and after an informal audition, became a member of the band without any explicit invitation, simply because "they just didn't ask him to leave." "Dave packed his kit into a large cardboard box and boarded a flight for Seattle, arriving on Friday, September 21, 1990."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Ultra-Deep Background on Dave Grohl: Part 2
facts.name: Dave Grohl

facts.title: Post-Scream Legal Issue (1990)
facts.body: After joining Nirvana and the band signed to DGC, Dave Grohl was sued for $40,000 by someone associated with Scream. This legal action alleged that Dave was still under contract to Scream due to an agreement he signed at some point during his time with them, even though Scream had already broken up. Fortunately, Dave had lawyers who were able to deal with the situation. "Dave was immediately sued by someone associated with Scream for $40,000 saying that he was still under contract to them, even though Scream had long broken up."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Ultra-Deep Background on Dave Grohl: Part 2
facts.name: Dave Grohl

facts.title: Grammy Boycott and Anti-Competition Stance (1990)
facts.body: When *I Do Not Want What I Haven't Got* was nominated for Grammys, Sinead boycotted the awards program, asserting, "I'm a punk, not a pop star. It shouldn't be a competition, it's about art." She made it a policy to refuse every award for which she was nominated or won, using the resulting controversy to draw attention to the issue of child abuse. "When I do not want what I haven't got was nominated for Grammys, she boycotted the awards program."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Sinead O'Connor

facts.title: Red Cross Donation and Move to England (1990)
facts.body: Following the negative backlash and accusations of "ungratefulness" for boycotting awards, Sinead donated her house in Hollywood to the Red Cross. This enabled a family of refugees from Somalia to live there, and she subsequently moved back to England. "She was so appalled at the way she was treated for this so-called ungratefulness that she gave her Hollywood house to the Red Cross."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Sinead O'Connor

facts.title: Star-Spangled Banner Controversy and Frank Sinatra Feud (1990)
facts.body: In 1990, Sinead declined to have "The Star-Spangled Banner" played before a show in New Jersey, which was misconstrued as a refusal to perform if it was played. Upon hearing this, Frank Sinatra famously declared his desire to "kick her in the ass." "And when Frank Sinatra heard that, he famously said he would like to, quote, kick her in the ass."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Sinead O'Connor

facts.title: Grammy Boycott (1990)
facts.body: When *I Do Not Want What I Haven't Got* was nominated for four Grammys, Sinéad O'Connor "very loudly boycotted" the award ceremony, stating that the Grammys and award shows were "nothing but a sham, an exploitation of artists." She demanded her name be withdrawn from all considerations, and it was. "She demanded that her name be withdrawn from all considerations. And it was."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Sinead O'Connor

facts.title: US Tour National Anthem Stance (1990)
facts.body: During a US tour in 1990, Sinéad O'Connor stated she would not perform anywhere if the American national anthem was played before her shows, leading to public controversy. "On a tour of the US in 1990, she let it be known that she would not perform anywhere that the American national anthem was played before her shows."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Sinead O'Connor

facts.title: Seismic Years of Transformation (1990-1991)
facts.body: The years 1990 and 1991 are described as "absolutely crucial" and "every bit as seismic" as the birth and rise of punk in 1976 and 1977 for the history of Alt Rock. This period marked a significant turning point, especially with the explosion of alternative music into the mainstream. "The years 1990 and 1991 are absolutely crucial to the history of Alt Rock. They are every bit as seismic as what we saw with the birth and rise of punk in 1976 and 1977."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Alt-rock

facts.title: Plagiarism Lawsuit by John Denver (1990)
facts.body: In 1990, New Order was successfully sued by folk singer John Denver for plagiarism over their song "Run," which was found to have similarities to Denver's song "Leaving on a Jet Plane." New Order did not contest the charges and settled out of court. "In 1990, John Denver, this cute little folk singer who looked like a muffet, nailed New Order with a plagiarism suit and won."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: New Order

facts.title: Major Label Signing and Influence on Nirvana (1990)
facts.body: The band signed a major record deal with DGC records in 1990, which was an unexpected move for an indie rock band. This deal was significant because Kurt Cobain of Nirvana, a big fan of Sonic Youth, saw it as proof that a band could maintain creative control even on a major label, leading Nirvana to sign with DGC. Thurston Moore himself had tipped DGC off to Nirvana's existence. "Sonic Youth shocked their contemporaries by signing a major record deal with DGC records, resulting in a record called GU. And it was because of this deal that DGC also got their hands on this little band called Nirvana."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Sonic Youth

facts.title: Major Label Signing to DGC (Spring 1990)
facts.body: Sonic Youth, known for being hard to sign, was in financial trouble by spring 1990. Geffen Records created a new subsidiary, DGC, specifically as an alternative label with an indie aesthetic and Geffen's distribution capabilities, targeting Sonic Youth as their first major signing. DGC guaranteed complete creative control, which convinced the band to sign, providing them with much-needed financial security. "And since DGC guaranteed the band, complete creative control over all aspects of their music, the band signed on the dotted line."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 8
facts.name: Sonic Youth

facts.title: Pirate Radio Broadcasts (1990)
facts.body: On September 1, 1990, The Cure attempted to debut a new album by setting up an unlicensed, illegal radio station called Cure FM from the roof of their manager's London office, distributing handbills that read "you can join in on the Cure's very own pirate party. Let's not go to bed." Technical difficulties marred the initial midnight broadcast, so they tried again on October 6th, broadcasting as Cure 102 at 101.7 FM with a five-hour show featuring interviews, reports, and tracks from their new remix album, Mixed Up. "The band had set up a pirate radio transmitter on the roof of their manager's office, hand bills in the passenger on the city that read, you can join in on the Cure's very own pirate party."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 2
facts.name: The Cure

facts.title: Attack on FM Revolver Offices (1990)
facts.body: On January 30, 1990, The Stone Roses launched a "grudge attack" on the offices of their former indie label, FM Revolver, and its president Paul Birch and his girlfriend Olivia, storming the premises with cans of blue and white paint. The incident, which caused $50,000 in damage to the offices and saw Birch's Mercedes vandalized with "free bodywork" and a brick through the windshield, led to the band's arrest the following day and subsequent vandalism charges; in March 1990, a judge fined each member $3,000 but spared them jail, fearing notoriety. "On January 30th, 1990, they launched a grudge attack on the offices of FM revolver president Paul Birch and his girlfriend, you know, just kind of teach him a lesson."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 2
facts.name: The Stone Roses

facts.title: Spike Island Performance (May 27, 1990)
facts.body: On May 27, 1990, The Stone Roses, hailed as one of the most important British rock bands, played their biggest gig at Spike Island, near Liverpool, on the Mersey River. The event attracted 30,000 "ecstasy field fans" to what was colloquially known as a toxic dump due to a nearby chemical factory causing chemical burns (mistaken for sunburn) and greasy residue in fans' hair. The Stone Roses headlined, coming on at 8 PM to a hero's welcome, marking a significant milestone as 30,000 people attended a concert by an indie band, an unprecedented achievement at the time. "Spike Island, the height of Madchester, the height of ecstasy mania, and the greatest moments in the career of one of the most important British rock bands of all time, the Stone Roses, playing Spike Islands, May 27, 1990."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 8
facts.name: The Stone Roses

facts.title: Spike Island Festival (1990)
facts.body: On May 27, 1990, The Stone Roses headlined an outdoor festival at Spike Island, a strip of heavily polluted land, drawing an unprecedented 30,000 people who paid about 14 quid each to enter. This massive turnout contrasted sharply with their struggles just twelve months prior to attract 30 people to a bar gig, highlighting their rapid ascent as an indie band. "A year later, May 27, 1990, the Roses had lined an outdoor festival on a strip of once heavily polluted land called Spike Island. Twelve months earlier, they were struggling to get 30 people to show up to a bar gig. This time, though, 30,000 people turned up, paying about 14 quid to get in."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Stone Roses

facts.title: Spike Island Concert (May 27, 1990)
facts.body: This outdoor concert at Spike Island, a peninsula in the Mersey River surrounded by chemical factories and power plants on a reclaimed chemical dump, was proclaimed "the gig of the year" upon its announcement. Despite being considered an "average or even below average" performance by the band, who seemed nervous and tentative, it drew their largest crowd (28,000-30,000 people). The event became legendary because it was a pivotal "meeting of the minds" for "Madchester kids" and "rave kids," fostered by ecstasy, and was heavily hyped by the British music press as the start of the 90s. "The line they took was, the 90s begin now. Ain't it great?"
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Stone Roses

facts.title: Reunion attempt with Mick Jones (1990)
facts.body: Around 1990, Mick Jones suggested reforming The Clash, but Joe Strummer's stubbornness prevented it. Joe insisted on the original late 70s/early 80s lineup (Joe, Mick, Paul Simonon, Topper Headon if sober, or Terry Chimes) and the return of former manager Bernie Rhodes, whom the other members refused to work with due to his past lawsuit attempt. "Joe was stubborn. He believed that if the clash were to rise again, it would have to be just as it was back in the late 70s and early 80s."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Joe Strummer

facts.title: Career Reboot - Grammy Win (1990)
facts.body: Bonnie Raitt's career underwent a dramatic transformation after her "Nick of Time" album won Album of the Year at the 1990 Grammy Awards, marking her as the "recording Academy's best Cinderella story." Prior to this, she had been toiling since the early 70s without a top 40 pop hit or top 20 LP, battling drug and alcohol addiction, from which she got sober in the late 80s. The Grammy win rebooted her career, turning her into a pop star at age 40, leading to consistent top 20 album chart placements and top 40 hits throughout the 90s. "You can literally divide Bonnie Rates' career into before she won the Grammy and after she won the Grammy."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.episode: And the Grammy Goes to… Edition Part 1
facts.name: Bonnie Raitt

facts.title: Andrew Wood's Death (March 19, 1990) – Heroin Overdose
facts.body: Andrew Wood, the popular singer of Mother Love Bone, died on Monday, March 19, 1990, the day before their album *Apple* was due for release. He was found comatose on March 16 after a heroin overdose, and after brain activity ceased, his family chose to take him off life support. "Andrew was a really popular guy, and he had lots of friends in Seattle. His death hit Chris Cornell, his old roommate particularly hard."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Mother Love Bone

facts.title: Frontman's Tragic Death (1990)
facts.body: Mother Love Bone, a band described as local heroes "poised for big things," had their dreams shattered when their frontman, Andrew Wood, died of a heroin overdose. His death occurred just days before their major label album was scheduled to be released, cutting short their potential rise. "Mother Lovevone, some local heroes that were poised for big things had their dreams shot to hell when frontman Andrew Wood died of a heroin overdose just days before their major label album was supposed to come out."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Mother Love Bone

facts.title: Decline by 1990-1991
facts.body: By 1990, hair metal, which had been strong for about eight years, was overexposed and tired. The proliferation of too many bands and an abundance of power ballads led to a dilution of quality and waning public interest. "It had been going strong for about eight years, but it was overexposed and tired."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Rumored Affair with David Bowie (1990)
facts.body: A rumor concerning an affair between Mick Jagger and David Bowie was ignited on the Joan Rivers show in 1990 by David's ex-wife, Angela Bowie. Jagger strongly denied the accusation, and David Bowie's lawyer issued a statement calling the implication "an absolute fabrication." The situation was further complicated by rumors that Angela Bowie and Mick Jagger might have had an affair while she was married to Bowie, leading some to believe the Rolling Stones song "Angie" was about her, though others suggested it was coded for David. "Jagger came up swinging, denying everything."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Mick Jagger

facts.title: Connecting Dave Grohl to Nirvana (1990)
facts.body: Buzz Osborne, a member of the Seattle band The Melvins, played a crucial role in Dave Grohl joining Nirvana. When Grohl, a friend, called him desperate for a drumming gig, Osborne, aware of Nirvana's drummer issues, provided him with the phone number of Nirvana's bassist, directly leading to Grohl's audition and recruitment. "Now Buzz was in a Seattle band called The Melvins, and Dave was hoping that he knew of any openings for a drummer. Now it just so happens that one of Buzz's friends was having drummer issues. He gave Dave the bass player's phone number."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 5
facts.name: The Melvins

facts.title: Buzz Osborne's Recommendation to Nirvana (1990)
facts.body: Buzz Osborne, a member of The Melvins and a figure "idolized by Kurt Cobain," played a pivotal role in Dave Grohl joining Nirvana. Osborne recommended Dave for the open drummer slot after Scream broke up, directly leading to Dave's audition and subsequent entry into Nirvana. "But then Buzz Osborne of the Melvins, a guy idolized by Kurt Cobain, recommended him for the open drummer slot with Nirvana."

facts.body: The title of this iconic song originated from an act of vandalism by Kathleen Hanna, a friend of Kurt Cobain and member of Bikini Kill. During a night of drinking in the winter of 1990, Hanna spray-painted "Kurt smells like teen spirit" on Cobain's bedroom wall in Olympia, Washington, referencing a trendy girls' deodorant used by Toby Vail (another Bikini Kill member whom Kurt liked). Kurt, who didn't wear deodorant, misinterpreted this as a compliment about embodying teenage rebellion, only learning the true, less profound inspiration after the song's writing, recording, and release. "It wasn't until after the song was written, recorded, and released that Kurt found out what had actually inspired one of the greatest rock and roll songs of all time."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 6
facts.name: Smells Like Teen Spirit

facts.title: Rehearsal Demo
facts.body: An early, raw rehearsal demo of this song from late 1990 or early 1991 was included in the *With the Lights Out* box set. This demo, which Kurt Cobain called "Smells Like Teen Spirit," featured their new drummer Dave Grohl and differed significantly from the final *Nevermind* version, being "almost a minute longer" with different words and arrangements. "It's a rehearsal demo of a new song that Kurt called Smells Like Teen Spirit. And it's one of the first things that featured their new drummer Dave Grohl."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Smells Like Teen Spirit

facts.title: Producer and Engineer for Sinead O'Connor (1990)
facts.body: Chris Birkett, who had previously mixed two singles from Sinead O'Connor's debut album, was contacted by Ensign Records executive Nigel Grainge to take over production for her second album, *I Do Not Want What I Haven't Got*. This occurred after Sinead walked out on the original producer, Nellee Hooper. Birkett described the recording process as bare-bones and worked closely with Sinead, notably producing her hit single "Nothing Compares 2 U." "So the vocal company phoned me up, and signed records, Nigel Brange. And he said that we've got the studio booked, and Shanade's got all the songs ready. We don't have a producer. Could you mind taking it over?"
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Chris Birkett
